messages:
acme-sre: Hey team — after our firewall changes last night our private VPC deployment in our colo (no-internet mode) started failing calls to the Redwood API. Getting TLS errors and occasional timeouts. We rolled back a rule and saw it recover briefly then fail again. Anyone seen this pattern?

maya: Sorry about the disruption — can you paste the exact error you see from the client and which endpoint you're hitting? Also are you using an outbound HTTP proxy or TLS-inspecting appliance? :thinking:

acme-sre: We go through a corporate proxy that does TLS inspect (BlueGate). Endpoint is api.redwood-inference.internal (we use split-horizon DNS that returns internal IPs). Error from our service logs: `x509: certificate is valid for bluegate.corp, not api.redwood-inference.internal` and sometimes `read tcp x.x.x.x:54321->y.y.y.y:443: i/o timeout`.

raj: That x509 message is classic TLS MITM from an intercepting proxy — the proxy presents its own cert (CN bluegate.corp). Two options: 1) Add the proxy CA to your service/trust store, or 2) configure the proxy to bypass TLS inspect for Redwood domains (SNI passthrough). Which is feasible in your environment?

acme-sre: We prefer bypass but the firewall team is strict. They only allow outbound by IP ranges (deny-by-default). We asked for Redwood IPs but they say IPs change and only allow long-lived prefixes.

anna: Quick note — since you're split-horizon resolving api.redwood-inference.internal to an internal IP, if your proxy does TLS inspect and rewrites SNI or does hostname re-write the cert verification will fail. If you can, run an s_client to confirm server cert chain before the proxy: `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal -showcerts` and compare to `openssl s_client -connect <proxy-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal` to see the interception.

acme-sre: Ran that. When I connect directly to the internal IP (bypassing proxy) we get Redwood cert with SANs: api.redwood-inference.internal, *.redwood-inference.internal. When we go through proxy it returns bluegate cert.

maya: OK — that confirms TLS inspect. Two follow-ups we usually recommend: 1) If firewall only allows IP-based egress rules, request the NAT/PAT egress IPs for your Redwood private deployment (we can provide your assigned egress IPs) so your team can allow them; 2) If intercept can't be disabled, install the proxy CA on the Redwood client hosts/truststore so the client trusts the proxy cert.

acme-sre: We asked for egress IPs and received an ambiguous note about CDN/backing storage hitting S3/google endpoints as well. Does Redwood require direct internet to public S3 endpoints? We're in no-internet mode so outbound to public cloud services is disallowed by policy.

maya: Short answer: Private deployments still need outbound connectivity for model layer and image pulls unless you use our air-gapped on-prem bundle. In your VPC-private mode we rely on pull model for weights and health-checks; that can hit object storage URLs that are on third-party providers. If you truly cannot reach the public internet we need to switch to our fully air-gapped packaging flow (requires ops coordination).

raj: For the firewall team: if you can accept DNS/FQDN allowlist rather than raw IP allowlist, you can permit `*.redwood-inference.internal`, `models.redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com` and `api.redwood-inference.external` (we'll provide canonical FQDNs). If only IPs are allowed, request the specific NAT egress IP block for your account — we have static egress ranges for Dedicated/Private customers on request.

acme-sre: Got it. Our next blocker is split-horizon DNS returning internal IPs that the proxy can't reach directly (proxy only routes internet). So sometimes requests go to internal IPs and never hit the proxy, causing timeouts. Any mitigation?

anna: Two mitigation approaches: 1) Make sure your proxy has routes to internal egress network (so proxy can reach internal IPs), or 2) change your split-horizon to return proxy-reachable addresses for hosts that must go via the proxy (i.e., return external-facing IPs). Also validate your internal firewall/NAT isn't dropping SYN/ACKs.

egress-probe-bot: automated probe results attached — 3 consecutive failures to api.redwood-inference.internal:443 from 10.12.0.5, handshake failed, TLS alert 40.

maya: To help debug quickly, please collect these and share: 1) `curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.internal:<port>:<internal-ip> https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health` output, 2) `openssl s_client -connect <internal-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal -showcerts` output, 3) tcpdump on the client showing 3-way handshake and TLS ClientHello/ServerHello (filter `host <internal-ip> and port 443`), 4) proxy logs for that session (if available).

acme-sre: Pasting curl + openssl snippets now.

acme-sre: ```
$ curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.internal:443:10.11.22.33 https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.internal (10.11.22.33) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* server certificate verification failed: certificate is not trusted
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) server certificate verification failed: certificate is not trusted
```

acme-sre: ```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.11.22.33:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=1 C = US, O = BlueGate, CN = BlueGate CA
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.redwood-inference.internal
   i:/CN=BlueGate CA
---
```

raj: That output again shows the proxy CA in the chain. Two parallel paths: ask network to add our provided egress IPs to the allowlist and exempt `api.redwood-inference.internal` from TLS inspect, or install the BlueGate CA to your service runtime truststore. Installing CA is quicker for immediate relief but may not be allowed by security.

acme-sre: Security won't allow adding our app runtime truststore change. We'll request egress IPs and TLS bypass exemption. Can Redwood give the exact NAT IPs AND a list of external storage hostnames we will need to allow? Also any temporary workaround to reduce client timeouts while we wait?

maya: Yes — we'll open a support ticket to provide your account's NAT egress IPs and canonical hostnames (models, metrics ingest, container registries). Temporary workaround: 1) ask network to route api.redwood-inference.internal traffic to a proxy-bypass path (internal route) so it doesn't hit TLS inspect, or 2) configure retries and increase client timeout to reduce impact while ops completes changes. Also enable request-level retries with idempotent endpoints.

anna: For the firewall team, sample tcpdump and packet details we need: `sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -w capture.pcap host 10.11.22.33 and port 443` and we need the proxy logs that show the request ID/timestamp. If you want, we can join a quick call to walk the NAT/route table. :hammer_and_wrench:

acme-sre: Thanks — we opened a change request for the firewall and submitted the support ticket. Will follow up with the capture and proxy logs. Appreciate the quick triage.

maya: Thanks — I'll attach the egress IPs and hostnames in the ticket and loop in our infra ops for air-gap options if needed. Keeping this thread updated. :thumbsup:
